stem:
$\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$ react at $25^{\circ}\text{C}$ to give $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$ as shown in the equation.

$$\text{NO(g)} + \text{NO}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2\text{O}_3\text{(g)} \qquad \Delta H = -7.2\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

The reaction is reversible and reaches equilibrium in a closed system.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Fig. 2.1 shows how the rate of the forward reaction changes with time.

Initially, the rate of the reverse reaction is zero.

Complete Fig. 2.1 to sketch how the rate of the **reverse** reaction changes with time.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

**Fig. 2.1**

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
State how the position of equilibrium changes, if at all, when the reaction takes place at $100^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Explain your answer.

Assume the pressure remains constant.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Table 2.1 shows the composition of an equilibrium mixture of $\text{NO(g)}$, $\text{NO}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3\text{(g)}$ at $101\text{ kPa}$.

**Table 2.1**

| gas | number of moles at equilibrium/mol |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{NO}$ | 0.605 |
| $\text{NO}_2$ | 0.605 |
| $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$ | 0.390 |

Calculate $K_{\text{p}}$, the equilibrium constant with respect to partial pressures.

Deduce the units of $K_{\text{p}}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Identify one natural process and one man-made process that cause the formation of atmospheric $\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: $\text{NO}_2$ is a brown gas that can be used to form nitric acid.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text:
$\text{NO}_2$ is a free radical.

Define free radical.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
$\text{NO}_2$ has a catalytic role in the oxidation of atmospheric sulfur dioxide.

Write equations to show the catalytic role of $\text{NO}_2$ in this oxidation.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text: State **one** environmental consequence of the oxidation of atmospheric sulfur dioxide.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: A student titrates nitric acid with a base to form a solution containing aqueous magnesium nitrate.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.text: Identify a base that the student could use.

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text:
The student evaporates the water to obtain magnesium nitrate solid. When this solid is heated it decomposes.

Write an equation for the decomposition of magnesium nitrate.

parts.label: (f)(iii)
parts.text: State how the thermal stability of Group 2 nitrates changes down the group.
